newsitem.title: USA: Clinton hails passage of chemical weapons treaty.
newsitem.headline: Clinton hails passage of chemical weapons treaty.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Thursday hailed the U.S. Senate's endorsement of a global treaty banning chemical weapons, saying it "served America well."

The Senate voted 74 to 26, more than the two-thirds majority needed to approve the pact, clearing the way for the United States to ratify the agreement known as the Chemical Weapons Convention before it goes into effect next Tuesday.

"This vote is an example of America working as it should -- Democrats and Republicans together, putting our country first, reaching across party lines, reaching for the common good," Clinton said at the White House after the vote.
He called the vote "vivid proof that we are stronger as a nation when we work together" and appealed to Republicans to join him in completing the job of balancing the U.S. budget.
Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott had appealed to Clinton to work with Republicans on the budget as they had with him on the treaty.

Clinton replied: "I'm willing to work through this process on the budget just the way we worked through this. If we can work together in a very practical way, to do what's in the national intersts, I think we can get there."
Clinton, who had a great deal of prestige both at home and abroad riding on the outcome of the vote, said he was profoundly grateful to the Senate.
"The U.S. Senate has served America well tonight," he said, adding that once again the United States had displayed the leadership it must demonstrate in building a safer world.

"Our troops will be less likely to face poison gas on the battlefield, our hand will be strengthened in the fight against terrorists and rogue states, we will end a century that began with the horror of chemical weapons in World War I much closer to the elimination of those kinds of weapons," Clinton said.
The treaty bans the development, production, stockpiling, transfer and use of chemical weapons, with the avowed purpose of ridding the world of them within 10 years.
